Cross-Strait Agreement on Investment Protection and Promotion (2012)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended effective 1 January 2025); Administrative Measures on Beneficial Ownership Information (PBOC and SAMR Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 November 2024); Measures for the Administration of Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing in Financial Institutions; Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the direct shareholder's jurisdiction (e.g., Ministry of Economic Affairs Department of Commerce, if the direct shareholder is formed in Taiwan; otherwise the relevant national corporate registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Apostille Convention state): notarization followed by Hague Apostille; no consular legalization. Path B (non-Apostille state): notarization followed by Consular Legalization at the competent PRC embassy or consulate; no apostille. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Apostille Convention state): notarization followed by Hague Apostille; no consular legalization. Path B (non-Apostille state): notarization followed by Consular Legalization at the competent PRC embassy or consulate; no apostille. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Apostille Convention state): notarization followed by Hague Apostille; no consular legalization. ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, UBOs, authorized signatories and beneficial counterparties against the OFAC SDN List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated List, and the domestic sanctions and counter-terrorism lists maintained by the People's Republic of China and Taiwan. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any politically exposed person, immediate family members or close associates; source of wealth and source of funds must be evidenced for every beneficial owner meeting the 25% threshold. Continuous negative-news monitoring, adverse-media checks, regulatory enforcement checks and conflict-of-interest assessments must be completed before incorporation, with re-screening every 90 days and escalation to the AML compliance officer within 24 hours of any positive hit.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform and Local Administration for

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Chapter II (Incorporation), Articles 2, 29, 32 and 47; Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (2019), Articles 4 and 28 with the Special Administrative Measures (Negative List, 2021 Edition); Implementing Rules of the Law on Protection of Investment by Taiwan Compatriots (2019 Amendment); Interim Regulations on the Administration of Registration of Market Entities (2021), Chapter II (Establishment Registration); Foreign Investment Information Reporting Measures (2019, as amended).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - the local Municipal/District Administration for Market Regulation at the WFOE registered office, acting through the National Integrated Online Administrative Service Platform for enterprise registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, accompanied by the Articles of Association, the Foreign Investment Initial Information Report, and the Legal Document Service Address Mandate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital applies to an e-commerce and automated dropshipping WFOE under the current Foreign Investment Negative List; the Sole Shareholder shall subscribe the full capital in the Articles of Association and must pay it in full within five years from incorporation pursuant to Article 47 of the Company Law (2023 Revision). No mandatory escrow account or government-designated guarantee account is required for capital contribution; the paid-in funds must be credited to the SAFE-registered foreign exchange capital account and applied to lawful corporate purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned Sole Shareholder acting by written resolution as the corporate organ of CN WFOE LTD hereby resolves: (1) the entire registered capital set out in the Articles of Association is subscribed and shall be paid in accordance with law; (2) the registered office located at the address stated in the Articles of Association is adopted as the statutory domicile for service and tax purposes; (3) the Legal Representative, Executive Director and Supervisor named in the appointment forms are appointed to hold office until replaced; (4) the designated formation agent is authorized to file the establishment registration with SAMR, open the capital contribution bank account and complete all post-incorporation filings; and (5) all formation expenditures are approved as company expenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise Name Self-Declaration and Investment Scope Pre-Screen
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR Local Market Regulation Administration online enterprise name declaration window on the National Integrated Online Administrative Service Platform.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the provincial integrated business formation portal, initiate enterprise name self-declaration by entering the proposed full name structure, and select a business scope limited to internet sales (excluding goods requiring licenses), domestic trade agency, and information services. The system performs an automated conflict check against registered and preliminarily approved names. Concurrently perform a Negative List (2021) self-assessment confirming that automated dropshipping retail is a permitted foreign-investment sector, thus allowing 100% indirect Taiwanese shareholding. The name reservation is valid for two months from approval.
required_dossiers: Proposed company names (3 to 5 alternatives)
Name self-declaration commitment letter
Electronic copy of shareholder identity or corporate identification
Pre-drafted business scope description compliant with the Negative List
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, resubmit using the system-generated alternatives or modify the trade name and re-file; a name dispute ruling may be requested under the name administration rules, and reapplication does not prejudice the formation timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Cross-Strait Verification of Taiwanese Investor Qualification Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan District Court Notary Office, Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF), Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) and its authorized notary verification bodies.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have the Sole Shareholder's identity document, and if a corporate investor, its business registration extract and board resolution to invest in the mainland, notarized by a Taiwan court notary. The original notarial certificate must be transferred through SEF to ARATS for document verification, and the verified copy submitted to the local SAMR, the designated capital account bank, and PRC legal counsel. The shareholder also executes a power of attorney in favor of the local formation agent after the verification is completed.
required_dossiers: Original notarized investor qualification certificate issued in Taiwan
SEF/ARATS cross-strait verification certificate
Taiwan Compatriot Permit and Taiwan resident credential
Executed power of attorney to the PRC formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notarial document is incomplete or defective, the ARATS verification office returns it with a written cure notice; the Taiwan notary must reissue the certificate and re-transfer it through SEF, and the corrected document is then accepted by SAMR and the receiving bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Establishment Registration and Initial Foreign Investment Information Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR Local Market Regulation Administration enterprise registration window and online fully-electronic registration system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Establishment Registration Application through the integrated online platform and complete electronic signing using the shareholder's bank digital certificate or electronic license app. Attach the Articles of Association complying with the mandatory provisions of the Company Law (2023 Revision), the verified Taiwanese investor documents, and the office address commitment. The system simultaneously collects the initial foreign investment information report for inclusion in the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System. Upon approval, the electronic Business License is issued immediately, and the paper license may be collected or couriered.
required_dossiers: Signed Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company
Articles of Association of a single-shareholder limited liability company
Verified shareholder qualification certificate and identity documents
Registered office proof or address commitment statement
Appointment documents and identity certificates of Legal Representative, Executive Director and Supervisor
Legal document service address mandate
Power of attorney appointing the filing representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any deficiency is communicated in a single written cure notice; the applicant may correct and resubmit online. If the registered scope touches a licensed sector, SAMR will issue a referral to the competent license authority. An adverse rejection may be appealed through administrative reconsideration or by resubmission fully cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Business License, Company Seal Engraving and Public Security Recordal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR Local Market Regulation Administration and Public Security Bureau-designated seal engraving service points.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Receive the electronic Business License and collect the paper original from the service window. Proceed to a Public Security-approved seal engraver to cut the company seal, financial seal, invoice seal and legal representative personal seal, and complete the mandatory seal recordal with the Public Security Bureau. Register the company seal specimen in the SAMR enterprise information system for subsequent banking and tax filings.
required_dossiers: Original and duplicate Business License
Taiwan Compatriot Permit and identity certificate of the Legal Representative
Seal engraving application stamped with the enterprise name approval notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If engraving data is erroneous, the designated engraver re-cuts the seal free of charge within one working day; delays in Public Security recordal do not suspend tax or bank processes and may be cured by presenting the engraving receipt.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Social Insurance, Banking, Customs and Foreign Exchange Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Tax Service (State Taxation Administration), Social Insurance and Housing Fund Centers, designated People's Bank of China licensed bank, State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through an authorized bank, and local Customs Houses.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of license issuance, complete tax registration on the electronic tax bureau, obtain the CA certificate and tax type determination, and register for payroll withholding. Open the basic deposit account and the foreign exchange capital account through a SAFE-authorized bank, and file the Foreign-Invested Enterprise Basic Information Registration and the capital account payment confirmation. If goods will be imported for dropshipping, register with Customs as an Import/Export Consignor and Recipient on the China International Trade Single Window and complete cross-border e-commerce enterprise type filing. Establish social insurance and housing fund contribution accounts for employees.
required_dossiers: Business License
Articles of Association and Negative List compliance statement
Identity certificates of Legal Representative and financial officer
Basic deposit account information and bank opening confirmation
Tax registration form and withholding agent registration
Customs registration application and corporate information sheet
Foreign-Invested Enterprise Basic Information Registration form processed by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late tax registration is curable through the first-violation non-penalty procedure or correction order; SAFE registration with incomplete documents may be accepted on a disparaging basis with a 5-working-day cure deadline; Customs filing is a recordal rather than licensing act and can be resubmitted through the Single Window if the system data error occurs.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: E-Commerce Operational Recordals and Physical Premises Safety and Environmental Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Communications Administration for ICP filing, SAMR online market regulation office, Local Ecology and Environment Bureau, and Fire and Rescue Squadron.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If a proprietary sales website or domain resolves to servers within the mainland, file the non-commercial Internet information service (ICP) recordal through the MIIT filing system and publish e-commerce business identity information under the E-Commerce Law. For the office and low-hazard warehousing premises, complete the fire protection acceptance recordal, the construction fire safety check where applicable, and the EIA registration form filing through the national EIA registration system. Confirm that pure self-operated dropshipping retail does not trigger the Value-Added Telecommunications (EDI) license, unless the WFOE later operates a third-party marketplace requiring such license.
required_dossiers: Domain name certificate and server hosting agreement
E-commerce operator compliance commitment letter
Fire safety inspection application or fire acceptance recordal form
EIA registration form filed online
Lease agreement and property ownership certificate
Identity certificate of the Legal Representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: An ICP filing rejection is cured by correcting the website content per the access provider's comments and resubmitting; fire safety defects require physical remediation and re-inspection; the EIA registration is instantly completed and, if selected for field inspection, must be rectified within 15 days as directed by the Ecology and Environment Bureau.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: SAMR Local Market Regulation Administration as the general industry regulator, the Ministry of Commerce E-Commerce and Informatization Department as the e-commerce policy authority, and the Local Ecology and Environment Bureau for environmental recordals.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business License with the approved business scope covering internet sales (excluding goods requiring licenses) and domestic trade agency; where a proprietary mainland-hosted website is operated, supplemented by the Non-Commercial Internet Information Service Filing number (ICP recordal). No dedicated dropshipping or e-commerce retail operating license is required for a self-operated retailer under the current Negative List.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China (MEE) acting through the Local Ecology and Environment Bureau.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: EIA Registration Form Filing (registration management category under the 2021 Classification List for Construction Project Environmental Impact Assessment; ordinary office and non-hazardous material warehousing does not require an EIA report or report sheet).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Domestic sewage must be discharged into the municipal network meeting the Grade 3 standard of GB 8978-1996 Integrated Wastewater Discharge Standard; no industrial wastewater is generated. Fugitive air emissions, if any, comply with GB 16297-1996; VOC control is limited to office fit-out and packaging materials in line with GB 50325-2020 indoor environmental quality limits. Solid waste and packaging are managed under the Solid Waste Pollution Prevention and Control Law (2020 Revision) with classified storage and transfer through qualified disposal entities, accompanied by electronic transfer vouchers; hazardous waste, such as waste batteries from returned goods, is stored per GB 18597-2001 and transferred to licensed recyclers.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: complete fire protection installation acceptance recordal for the leased office and warehouse under the Fire Protection Law (2021, Articles 10 and 13) and, where the premises fall within public assembly use, obtain the pre-opening fire safety inspection or commitment-based check by the Fire and Rescue Squadron. Construction safety: complete housing rental recordal and structural load verification for mezzanine or racking areas in the warehouse. Occupational health: carry out occupational hazard project filing under the Law on Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases (simple filing for low-hazard e-commerce warehousing), with basic dust and noise personal protective equipment. Work safety: prepare the emergency response plan and file it with the local Emergency Management Bureau, and register and periodically inspect any special equipment, such as lifts or forklifts, with the market regulation special equipment authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (財政部) and its subordinate regional National Taxation Bureaus (各地區國稅局), including the National Taxation Bureaus of Taipei, Northern, Central, Southern, and Kaohsiung areas, depending on the company's registered office. The principal online portals are the Ministry of Finance website (https://www.mof.gov.tw), the E-Tax Integrated Portal (https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw), and the e-Invoice Integrated Service Platform (https://www.einvoice.nat.gov.tw).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-invested Taiwan WFOE (limited liability company) first obtains foreign investment approval from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs under the Foreign Investment Act and incorporates with the Ministry of Economic Affairs through the Company Registration One-Stop Service. The incorporation process yields the company registration certificate and a statutory eight-digit Unified Business Number (統一編號), which functions as the corporate tax identification number, the business tax (VAT) registration number, and the e-invoice identifier. The WFOE must then complete profit-seeking enterprise income tax registration and business tax registration with the competent local National Taxation Bureau before commencing business, filing the company registration certificate, articles of incorporation, the responsible person's identification, corporate seal, and registered office address. The National Taxation Bureau will issue a tax registration certificate and approve the purchase and use of Uniform Invoices (統一發票). Subsequently, the WFOE obtains a company digital certificate (工商憑證) and enrolls in the e-Invoice Turnkey transmission service for electronic filing and electronic invoice issuance. No minimum paid-in capital is required under the current Company Act, and the entire registration procedure is typically completed within 15 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Taiwan does not operate a check-the-box entity classification election; an incorporated WFOE limited company is mandatorily taxed at the entity level as a profit-seeking enterprise with worldwide income taxation under the Income Tax Act. Available statutory elections relevant to the cross-border automated dropshipping structure include: (i) election of a non-calendar fiscal year subject to approval by the National Taxation Bureau; (ii) election under the Foreign Investment Act route which governs foreign-investor registration and may affect tax-treaty benefits; (iii) election to file joint consolidated income tax returns for relation-enterprise groups under the Income Tax Act if strict affiliated-group criteria are met; (iv) election to register voluntarily as a full value-added Business Tax taxpayer for a small-scale business otherwise taxed on deemed sales at the special 1% rate; and (v) election to transmit e-invoices directly through the Turnkey channel or indirectly through an accredited e-invoice value-added center. Hybrid mismatch and CFC/PEM rules are not elective; they apply by statute and require self-assessment and disclosure where controlled foreign corporations or place-of-effective-management re-characterization is triggered.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax (加值型及非加值型營業稅法), commonly referred to as Taiwan Business Tax or VAT, with a value-added regime for most goods and services and special non-value-added regimes for certain financial services and small-scale enterprises.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Full VAT registration with Uniform Invoice (統一發票) obligations is mandatory when a Taiwan-resident profit-seeking enterprise has average monthly taxable sales of NT$200,000 or more (approximately NT$2.4 million annualized). Businesses below this threshold are generally treated as small-scale enterprises and assessed on tax-authority-determined deemed sales at a special 1% business tax rate, with no entitlement to input VAT credits. Separately, a foreign electronic-service supplier without a Taiwan fixed place of business becomes registrable and must collect 5% Business Tax on online services supplied to Taiwan individuals once annual taxable sales exceed NT$480,000. All Taiwan WFOEs, including those in the automated dropshipping industry, must complete business tax registration before commencing business regardless of turnover volume.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates Uniform Invoices (統一發票) for all standard VAT taxpayers. Electronic Uniform Invoices (電子發票) must be transmitted to the Ministry of Finance e-Invoice Integrated Service Platform (EISP) through the direct Turnkey channel or an accredited e-invoice value-added center, using XML file formats and a company digital certificate (工商憑證). Under the current administrative framework, B2B e-invoice data is generally required to be uploaded to the EISP within 48 hours of issuance, while B2C e-invoice data may be uploaded within the bi-monthly filing period. The EISP performs automated validation, rejects non-conforming records, and records platform receipt codes. There is no pre-issuance fiscal-stamping or real-time clearance requirement equivalent to the Italian SDI or similar Latin American fiscal control regimes, but retail sales to consumers must carry a QR code and participate in the Uniform Invoice lottery system. Marketplace and dropshipping platforms operating in Taiwan may be recognized as e-invoice transmitters for their sellers and are then required to provide API integration for real-time or periodic invoice data upload to the EISP.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act, the 0% Business Tax rate applies to: (i) the export of goods from the Taiwan customs territory; (ii) services provided in Taiwan and used outside Taiwan, or services rendered and used wholly outside Taiwan; and (iii) certain sales of goods within duty-free areas and between foreign buyers in triangular export arrangements. For the automated dropshipping business model, zero-rating eligibility requires the Taiwan WFOE to evidence either: (a) for goods physically exported from Taiwan to the foreign end-customer, that the WFOE appears as the exporter/consignor on the Customs Export Declaration and holds transport documentation showing delivery abroad; or (b) for goods shipped directly from a third-country supplier (for example, mainland China) to the foreign end-customer without entering Taiwan, that the transaction is a triangular export under which the WFOE zero-rates only the cross-border merchandising service or commission income, supported by the supplier's export declarations, cross-border transport evidence, and the WFOE's receipt of foreign currency proceeds. Excess input VAT credits attributable to such zero-rated exports may be refunded on a bi-monthly filing basis, subject to tax-authority verification against customs EDI records, e-invoice data, foreign-exchange settlement data, and retained documentary evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口報單) naming the Taiwan WFOE as exporter/seller and evidencing departure from Taiwan customs territory
Commercial Invoice and Packing List expressly indicating 0% Business Tax treatment
Ocean Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or courier shipment receipt (for example, DHL, UPS, FedEx, EMS) evidencing physical delivery to the foreign consignee
Inward Foreign Exchange Remittance Certificate (外匯收入水單) or bank settlement certificate showing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
Sales Contract or Purchase Order from the foreign buyer establishing the commercial terms of the export sale

For triangular/offshore dropshipment: the third-country supplier's export declaration, cross-border transport records, and shipment tracking evidencing direct delivery from the third-country warehouse to the foreign end-customer without entry into Taiwan
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to intensive audit verification against Taiwan Customs EDI export declarations, e-Invoice Integrated Service Platform records, transport waybills, and the Central Bank foreign-exchange settlement database. Where a zero-rating claim is unsupported, overstated, or fraudulent, the National Taxation Bureau will retrospectively reverse the 0% rate, assess 5% Business Tax on the full export consideration, and impose a delinquency surcharge of up to 15% plus statutory interest. Under Article 51 of the Business Tax Act, the tax authority may levy an evasion penalty of up to three times the underpaid tax. The general tax assessment period is five years for filed returns and seven years for unfiled returns, permitting significant retroactive clawback. Fraudulent export zero-rating involving forged customs documents or fabricated foreign-exchange remittance certificates is additionally subject to criminal tax evasion liability under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act, carrying imprisonment of up to five years, and the responsible person, including the WFOE director, may be held personally liable for civil penalties and surcharges. In egregious cases, the tax authority may suspend the taxpayer's Uniform Invoice purchase entitlement and e-invoice transmission privileges while the investigation is pending.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese renminbi (CNY) is not fully freely convertible under the capital account. Current-account transactions, including cross-border e-commerce sales of goods and associated logistics and payment service fees, operate under a verified-positivity framework that permits conversion via designated foreign-exchange (FX) banks subject to SAFE record-filing and documentary verification. Profit remittance by a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) is treated as a capital-account current-item outbound transfer: it requires prior audited financial statements, corporate income tax (CIT) settlement and withholding certificates, and verification that the enterprise has completed statutory foreign-exchange registration (FDI registration), annual multi-department reporting, and SAFE capital-project information reporting. WFOEs are prohibited from direct conversion of registered capital into RMB for purposes other than bona fide business use under the 2014 Circular on Further Improving the Administration of Foreign Exchange in Capital Projects and related SAFE operational rules. Capital-account items, including foreign debt and equity transfers, require separate SAFE approvals or registrations. For an automated dropshipping WFOE with no physical goods inventory in China, the key remittance hurdle is evidencing that underlying sales transactions represent genuine current-account trade in goods or services, supported by customs declarations where applicable, online platform sales reports, logistics delivery records, payment provider settlement statements, and complete invoice documentation, in order to satisfy the bank's 'real trade background' verification and SAFE's anti-fraud and anti-money-laundering checks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the current SAFE framework, China has abolished the mandatory full surrender of export proceeds in foreign currency. Export receipts in FX may be retained by the WFOE in its designated FX settlement account at a domestic bank, or converted into RMB voluntarily. However, all export proceeds for goods must be repatriated to China within the statutory time limit: the general requirement is that export proceeds must be received and settled through the domestic banking system no later than 180 days from the date of export declaration, unless a longer period is approved by SAFE or the relevant goods are eligible for a deferred payment arrangement under SAFE regulations. There is no mandatory conversion ratio in 2025; the enterprise may keep FX proceeds in an interest-bearing current account or convert to RMB through a domestic bank at the market-based central parity rate with a daily spread determined by the PBOC. Nevertheless, the WFOE must complete the electronic 'trade in goods' declaration (货物贸易外汇收支名录登记) under SAFE's goods-trade foreign-exchange administration, and each receipt from an overseas buyer or an online payment intermediary such as Stripe or PayPal remitting the proceeds must be matched against the corresponding customs declaration or postal/express shipment record. Proceeds from cross-border e-commerce retail sales may be settled under the simplified 'cross-border e-commerce retail export' procedures where the total value per shipment is below a stated threshold (typically USD 5,000 or equivalent), requiring a qualified third-party payment institution or the bank to handle the settlement and maintain transaction-level records. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day window, or failure to report the credit to SAFE, may result in administrative penalties, mandatory correction orders, inclusion in the foreign-exchange violation list, and suspension of the bank's processing of future transactions.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low-Medium (legally restricted). Foreign fintech or electronic money institutions (EMIs) incorporated outside mainland China are not permitted to open deposit accounts with Chinese commercial banks in their own right without a licensed Chinese banking or payment institution entity. A non-resident EMI cannot provide a physical or fully digital settlement account in CNY inside mainland China unless it operates through a licensed Chinese third-party payment institution (e.g., Alipay, WeChat Pay, or a licensed cross-border payment processor) under PBOC/SAFE rules. Offshore EMI accounts used to collect payments from customers (e.g., Stripe account with a Hong Kong or Singapore entity) may coexist with the mainland WFOE, but the WFOE's own export proceeds must ultimately be repatriated to its mainland bank account via a lawful cross-border payment channel. Using an offshore EMI solely to collect dropshipping revenue outside China, without a compliant underlying economic substance and tax reporting chain, would create permanent establishment and transfer pricing risks in Taiwan/China and fail the SAFE real-trade-background test. Practical viable structure: (i) an overseas payment intermediary licensed by the country of the sales platform (e.g., Stripe, PayPal) collects the end-customer funds; (ii) the intermediary, or the WFOE's mainland partner/PingPong, WorldFirst, or LianLian pay-type licensed service provider, settles the funds to the WFOE's domestic settlement account under a SAFE-filed cross-border e-commerce receivable collection scheme; (iii) the WFOE maintains quarterly reconciliation between platform payouts and its own accounting records. Foreign EMIs cannot directly clear RMB funds in CIPS/CHIPS or SWIFT for mainland corporations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence and in-person KYC interview are effectively mandatory for opening accounts used by a mainland WFOE under the prevailing PBOC 'real-name account management' and commercial bank risk practices. The legal representative (or the authorised person under a notarised and legalised power of attorney) must be physically present at the bank counter to complete the account opening interview in the jurisdiction where the bank branch is located; banks require the company's original business license (three-in-one social credit code), articles of association, capital verification report or paid-in-capital proof, leasing contract of the actual business premises, and the original identity documents of the legal representative and all UBOs owning more than 25% equity. For a newly incorporated WFOE with zero minimum capital and automated dropshipping operations, banks operate a stricter 'beneficial owner identification, actual business place inspection, and transaction volume forecast' process. Remote or fully digital onboarding is not permitted for a local-currency corporate current account: a PBOC branch may not be involved, but commercial banks' internal AML/KYC policies routinely require an in-person visit after the account is opened. Foreign non-resident directors who are not physically in China may own the WFOE, but the legal representative must be an actual person resident in China or present at the bank interview, because Chinese banks will not accept remote video-only KYC for a new corporate account where the legal representative is a non-resident with no Chinese visa or no verifiable address. Some banks, such as the Bank of China, offer 'account opening via enterprise online pre-registration' plus a one-time physical visit by the legal representative or the financial controller to the branch. We categorise the mandate as: 'Physical presence of the legal representative or a properly authorised senior manager is mandatory; a remote opening is impossible unless a Chinese-resident legal representative is appointed and the bank accepts a power-of-attorney arrangement with a bank officer verified by video call, which is rare and strictly case-by-case.'

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A newly incorporated WFOE with zero minimum registered capital and a pure cross-border dropshipping model triggers the bank's 'high-risk impersonal online sales' red flag; the bank sees no fixed asset base, no local payroll, and no existing transaction history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) notarised and certified Articles of Association reflecting the WFOE's legitimate e-commerce purpose; (ii) three-dimensional business substance evidence: a valid office lease agreement of at least 12 months in a reputable commercial building, photos, utility bills, and an on-site employee or liaison; (iii) a detailed business plan and cash-flow forecast consistent with ISIC 4791 automated dropshipping; (iv) executed master agreements with payment service providers (Stripe / PayPal / licensed Chinese cross-border payer), the upstream suppliers, and end-customer-facing platforms; (v) platform credentials showing active or pending sales listings in the target markets; (vi) audited or management accounts, if any, and an undertaking to submit monthly financial statements; and (vii) a compliance manual covering AML/CFT, sanctions screening, and adverse-media checks of suppliers and customers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The beneficial owners and directors are often non-Taiwan-resident or non-mainland-resident natural persons, creating a 'no local natural-person control' and 'unclear source of funds' red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) full chain of ownership from each UBO down to the WFOE, with notarised identity documents, passports, and proof of residential address; (ii) source-of-wealth declarations supported by bank statements, tax returns, or salary/purchase-agreement documentation for the capital injection; (iii) a notarised power of attorney appointing a Chinese-resident finance manager or legal representative who can attend interviews and sign bank documents; (iv) corporate registry extracts from Taiwan and China showing good standing; (v) personal and corporate reference letters from existing bankers in the investor's jurisdiction; (vi) confirmations that no PEP or sanctions exposure exists; and (vii) the WFOE's ultimate parent company's audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected payment rails (Stripe / PayPal) and the high transaction velocity of dropshipping are viewed as generating unresolved third-party payments and non-face-to-face customers; banks fear the account will be used for money laundering or fraudulent e-commerce schemes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) a detailed explanation of the end-to-end payment flow, showing that funds are collected by Stripe/PayPal in the name of the WFOE (wholly owned by the same legal entity) rather than by third parties; (ii) a signed merchant agreement with Stripe/PayPal demonstrating KYC already undertaken; (iii) a reconciliation policy requiring that each settlement from the payment provider is matched to the underlying sales order and logistics tracking number; (iv) sample transaction records and order-management system screenshots illustrating transparent traceability from customer purchase to supplier fulfilment to payment settlement; (v) a written AML/CFT programme adapted to e-commerce, including transaction monitoring for sudden spikes, refunds to non-original payment methods, and sanctions screening of customer IP addresses; (vi) a commitment to quarterly external compliance audits; and (vii) the bank's own e-commerce account package, which accepts cross-border settlement under the 'trade in goods' declaration scheme.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The need to convert incoming FX proceeds and pay overseas suppliers triggers the bank's 'non-matching trade background' query, especially for dropshipping where goods may never enter mainland China and the customs declaration may only be made by the outbound shipper or the marketplace consolidated customs filer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) the SAFE '货物贸易外汇管理' registration code (名录登记) proving the WFOE is a qualified goods trade entity; (ii) a complete contract chain: purchase order from final consumer to the WFOE, sales order from the WFOE to the upstream supplier, and payment request from the supplier; (iii) customs electronic data from the outbound post/express operator or e-commerce platform showing the export declaration number, package tracking, and declared value, especially if the WFOE uses the '跨境电子商务零售出口' simplified declaration scheme through a licensed customs broker; (iv) payment service provider settlement statements and the corresponding Swift MT103 or bank credit advices; (v) a comparison table matching each shipment's tracking number to the sale amount and the remittance received; (vi) logistics agreements with the express carrier or warehouse operator utilising a mainland bonded warehouse or Hong Kong consolidation centre; (vii) if goods are drop-shipped from outside China, obtain a customs broker opinion or a written statement from the tax bureau confirming the transaction is a service/brokerage or cross-border sale, and ensure the invoice issued is appropriate (e.g., a zero-rated export invoice or a service invoice); and (viii) a formal undertaking that all FX proceeds will be repatriated to the mainland within 180 days and that any mismatch will be reported proactively.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The registered capital is 'false-capital' or zero (minimum capital requirement officially false but banks often require a capital injection to prove substance), leading the bank to classify the enterprise as 'empty-shell enterprise with no equity investment'.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) proof of payment-in of paid-in capital, even a minimal amount of USD 10,000-RMB 100,000, in the form of a capital contribution wire from the shareholder's overseas bank account to the capital account (资本金账户), accompanied by a capital verification report by a certified public accountant; (ii) the SAFE FDI registration certificate and the bank's capital account instruction; (iii) a cash-flow budget showing that the capital injection will cover three months of operating expenses and initial platform fees; (iv) if the bank requires a higher minimum, negotiate a 'business plan driven' assessment and request an exception with the bank's SME e-commerce unit; and (v) an explanation of the statutory zero-minimum-capital rule with a reference to the 'Provisions on the Administration of Foreign-Invested Enterprises' and the negative list, showing that a retail e-commerce WFOE is not subject to a minimum capital requirement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant route for a Taiwan parent to inject capital into a mainland WFOE is as follows: (1) register the FDI project with the local counterpart of the Ministry of Commerce (外商投资信息报告) and obtain the SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration for FDI; (2) open a RMB or FCY capital account (资本金账户) at a designated bank; (3) wire the injection from the Taiwan shareholders' bank account via SWIFT using purpose code 'FDI Equity Injection' (and for the PBOC, the remittance instruction should reference 'Investment in the capital of a resident enterprise' (股权投资), commonly using the e-Code 'TWC' or 'Foreign Direct Investment' as specified by the bank) with a PDF of the FDI registration certificate and the board resolution approving the capital; (4) the receiving bank performs the SAFE 'permitted use' verification; (5) the funds may be credited to the RMB settlement account after conversion under the 'FDI capital project settlement' regime, and the WFOE must use the funds strictly for operating costs, procurement, salaries, rents, and other non-prohibited activities; (6) file the quarterly 'FDI report' with SAFE through the bank, and include the capital injection in the annual multi-department reporting (工商年报). No in-principle approval from SAFE is required because China applies a 'registration-based' system for FDI; however, remittances of more than RMB 5 million (or the bank's internal threshold) will trigger an enhanced review of the source of funds. Wire transfer protocols applicable: use SWIFT MT103, ensure the beneficiary account name exactly matches the WFOE's bank-account name, provide the full legal name and tax identification number of the sender, and include the 8-character FX business code (e.g., 'FDI', '622') determined by the bank; for payment institutions, a special remarks field '跨境电商收结汇' is used when converting sales proceeds, not for capital injections. Verification required: the bank will check the board resolution, the foreign-invested enterprise business license, the SAFE FDI file, and a declaration that the capital is not from a sanctioned jurisdiction. If the Taiwan parent uses an intermediary company (e.g., a Hong Kong vehicle), the FDI route must still show the ultimate investor, and an additional '实际控制人说明' may be required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound disbursements from the WFOE to overseas suppliers (e.g., the dropshipping upstream vendor in the Taiwan region or a third-country manufacturer), the permitted clearing rails are as follows: (i) Direct SWIFT MT103 payment: the WFOE instructs its domestic bank to transfer RMB or FX funds to the supplier's account; the bank requires a verified trade background — an import/export contract or purchase order, a supplier invoice, customs or logistics evidence, and, where the goods are purchased from outside mainland China, an import customs declaration if the goods physically pass through customs; if goods are drop-shipped directly from a third-country factory to an overseas customer and never legally enter mainland China, the payment may be re-characterised as a cross-border service payment or offshore purchase, with the WFOE as the seller of services/merchandise, requiring a service-buying agreement, tax invoice, and possibly a tax withholding by the bank. (ii) Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C): a confirmed, irrevocable L/C issued by the WFOE's bank may be used for higher-value purchases; for dropshipping, it is rarely used due to low unit values and high volumetric frequency, but for bulk replenishment of inventory in an overseas bonded warehouse, an L/C at sight is acceptable. (iii) Banker's acceptance or T/T after goods receipt: the common e-commerce practice is 'T/T against order invoice' within 30 days. All outbound payments are subject to the bank's real-trade-background verification; the bank will check the commodity code, price reasonableness, and recipient jurisdiction. Under SAFE and PBOC rules, the WFOE cannot use its own RMB operating funds to buy FX for an overseas payment unless it has an approved current-account FX purchase quota; in practice the bank processes each application individually. To ensure smooth settlements, the WFOE must maintain a digital repository of supplier agreements, proof-of-delivery, and a transaction list to reconcile the outbound payment with the corresponding sales funds collected from Stripe/PayPal. MT103 fields should include the beneficiary bank's SWIFT BIC, the beneficiary account, and the purpose code 'Trade Payment' as instructed by the bank. The Commercial L/C route requires the WFOE to deposit margin (typically 10%-50%) and the bank will check the WFOE's credit line, history, and KYC profile.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNY/USD forwards (远期结售汇) with a licensed domestic bank: permitted for hedging genuine current-account FX exposures arising from cross-border e-commerce sales, subject to the bank's assessment of a real trade background and the SAFE rule that the forward must mature within the underlying trade period and be closed out against actual FX cash flows.

CNY/USD FX swaps (货币掉期), also known as cross-currency swaps, permissible between a domestic bank and the WFOE for matching cash flows on capital accounts or large trade transactions, subject to bank credit approval and SAFE reporting.

Offshore NDF (non-deliverable forward) contracts: theoretically permissible for the Taiwan parent or an offshore treasury centre, but the mainland WFOE cannot directly enter an NDF with an offshore counterparty without having a genuine offshore trade receivable/payable and using an offshore account; many banks caution that onshore WFOEs are better served by participating in the onshore deliverable forward market, because an NDF may be treated as a disguised capital-flow vehicle and violate SAFE Circular 7 of 2017 regarding real-trade-backed FX derivatives.

FX options (买入看跌或看涨期权): available from domestic banks for hedging currency risk, but stricter for SMEs with no existing FX positions; the purchase must be real-trade-backed; only plain-vanilla options are permitted, and option strategies that increase leverage may be denied.

Cross-border RMB settlement swap agreements (跨境人民币资金池): not a classic hedging instrument but a permissible liquidity tool for a group treasury; if the WFOE is part of a cross-border group, a two-way cross-border RMB cash-pooling arrangement with a domestic permitted bank in the pilot zone may reduce FX conversion needs.

Natural hedging through multi-currency accounts: maintaining USD, EUR, or CNY current accounts at the domestic bank and offsetting payables against receivables in the same currency to reduce conversion frequency, permissible without SAFE approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Settlement Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Republic of China (Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 May to 31 May of the year following the relevant calendar tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a delayed-filing fee (滯報金) of 10% of the tentative tax, minimum NT$1,500 and maximum NT$30,000; filing only after replacement assessment triggers a 怠報金 of 20%, minimum NT$3,000 and maximum NT$90,000. Underpayment attracts an additional penalty up to 10% of the underpaid tax plus statutory interest; wilful evasion carries criminal tax liability and, after rectification notices and six months of business inactivity, an administrative dissolution order by the Company Registrar as the strike-off analogue.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Withholding Statements for salaries, rent, royalties, and independent-contractor fees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: District National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January of the year following the year in which the payments were made
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs administrative fines up to NT$15,000; failure to issue payee statements forfeits payroll-expense deductions; wilful under-withholding subjects the company to collection of the full shortfall, interest, and a tax-evasion penalty up to three times the evaded amount, and persistent non-compliance can support a registry-initiated dissolution order after a six-month inactivity test.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign and PRC-Invested Enterprise Annual Operation Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 June for the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 30-day rectification notice is issued for late or missing filings; continued omission blocks dividend repatriation, capital remittance, and new investment approvals; two consecutive missing years justify revocation of the investment permit, whereupon the Company Registry may commence dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder approval of financial statements, business report, and profit-appropriation resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records retained at the registered office and available for inspection by the Company Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of fiscal year-end, i.e., by 30 June for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The competent authority may issue a rectification order and fine the responsible director up to NT$50,000 per violation; unresolved non-approval for a full year exposes directors to personal civil liability for improper distributions and may support a dissolution order based on shareholder deadlock.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership, shareholder register, and statutory register audit metadata
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company Registry, Commercial and Enterprise Agency, Ministry of Economic Affairs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: reconfirmed by 30 June each year; any share transfer or UBO change filed within 15 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or false UBO filings attract administrative fines up to NT$500,000 under the Money Laundering Control Act plus a rectification order; deliberate concealment may carry criminal sanctions; a persistent two-year filing default is treated as administrative non-cooperation and can trigger registry-initiated dissolution proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent CPA audit is compulsory for public companies and for a closely held limited company when paid-in capital reaches NT$30 million, when outstanding credit from financial institutions reaches NT$30 million, when annual gross operating revenue plus non-operating income reaches NT$100 million for income-tax filing purposes, or when the company is otherwise designated by the Financial Supervisory Commission or the Ministry of Economic Affairs.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies apply Taiwan-endorsed IFRS; the closely held WFOE applies the Business Accounting Act and the SME-oriented Enterprise Accounting Standards (企業會計準則公報), with tax-basis adjustments reflected in the annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax settlement return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For this automated-dropshipping WFOE, the UBO confirmation follows a layered Taiwan protocol: (i) the PRC/foreign investing company and each natural or legal person owning, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of the capital or exercising effective control must be registered in the beneficial-ownership statement filed with the Company Registry; (ii) any transfer of membership or control change requiring Investment Commission clearance must be pre-approved and then filed in the statutory register and UBO platform within 15 days; (iii) at each annual shareholder approval, by 30 June, the responsible person must reconfirm the UBO schedule and reconcile it against the share register, directors' register, and minute book; and (iv) the complete set of registers must remain available at the registered office for on-site inspection by the Company Registry and anti-money-laundering authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book
